script_block.paragraph: HMS Argus (I49) was a British aircraft carrier with a displacement of 14,700 tons, an overall length of 565.0 ft, and a beam of 68.0 ft. Argus evaluated various types of arresting gear, general procedures needed to operate a number of aircraft in concert and fleet tactics. Argus was recommissioned and partially modernised shortly before the Second World War and served as a training ship for deck-landing practice until June 1940. By 1942, the Royal Navy was very short of aircraft carriers, and Argus was pressed into front-line service despite her lack of speed and armament.
